findings.title: Silence notifications is a no-op for Prometheus-only list items
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, and AlertRuleMenu exposes Silence notifications using that rule's permissions. Clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer, but the drawer is still rendered only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true (lines 104–105). Since rule is undefined for every Grafana rule in the new list, no drawer opens. Adapt the drawer flow to load the necessary ruler data on demand or support the Prometheus rule.

findings.title: Removing rulerRule also removes Pause and Delete actions
findings.body: This list item now passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons. Although AlertRuleMenu computes pause and delete abilities from promRule, its Pause item still requires a Grafana rulerRule and its Delete item still requires rulerRule to exist. Consequently authorized users can no longer pause, resume, or delete rules from either the grouped or filtered Grafana list. These actions need an identifier-based flow or on-demand ruler loading rather than silently disappearing.

findings.title: skipToken does not actually disable Grafana abilities
findings.body: Passing skipToken converts the rule to undefined but still returns the abilities computed by useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. For an undefined rule, loading is false, duplicateSupported is true, and Duplicate is allowed whenever the user has Grafana rule-create permission. AlertRuleMenu calls this hook with skipToken for datasource rules and ORs its result with the datasource abilities. This exposes Duplicate for datasource rules even when their ruler is unavailable or the user lacks external rule-create/write permission. Return unsupported/disallowed abilities when the token is supplied.

findings.title: Preserve federated-group immutability in the CombinedRule hook
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), but now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false. Existing CombinedRule consumers therefore treat Mimir groups with source_tenants as ordinary editable groups and enable Update/Delete for users with external write permission. This removes the explicit protection against modifying federated rules through flows that do not support federation. Preserve the group-level federation check when adapting the legacy hook.
